blocks: Fast static-analysis tool that finds bugs and security issues by matching lightweight, syntax-aware patterns over code. Rules are written as data in YAML, where $X metavariables capture a subexpression and can be reused within the same rule; rules install from a registry, and no user code is required.
Descends from sgrep, written by Yoann Padioleau as part of the pfff library, and renamed Semgrep in 2020.
Written in OCaml, with a Python CLI.
Developer-tools and application-security company behind Semgrep. Founded in 2017 as r2c by Isaac Evans, Drew Dennison, and Luke O'Malley, later renamed Semgrep, Inc.
Ships Semgrep and a hosted AppSec platform built around it.

Text-based semigraphics, pseudographics, or character graphics is a primitive method used in early text mode video hardware to emulate raster graphics without having to implement the logic for such a display mode.

There are two different ways to accomplish the emulation of raster graphics. The first one is to create a low-resolution all points addressable mode using a set of special characters with all binary combinations of a certain subdivision matrix of the text mode character size; this method is referred to as block graphics,1(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semigraphicscite_note-1) or sometimes mosaic graphics.

The second one is to use special shapes instead of glyphs (letters and figures) that appear as if drawn in raster graphics mode, sometimes referred to as semi- or pseudo-graphics; an important example of this is box-drawing characters.
